items.summary: arXiv:2611.32386v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Wireless communication networks are expanding from mere information transfer to sensing: in the Integrated Sensing and Communication paradigm, existing infrastructure and signals are reused to capture physical information about the surroundings of devices, envisioned to inform high-stakes applications such as healthcare and autonomous vehicles. items.summary: arXiv:2611.32780v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are transforming recommender systems into content-aware decision systems. items.title: Enabling Verifiable Output Lineage for Virtualized ML Workload Execution
items.summary: arXiv:2611.28344v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Machine learning (ML) property attestation lets a model provider demonstrate properties of their models and datasets to verifiers, and trusted execution environments (TEEs) have emerged as its most practical mechanism. items.title: Real Package, Wrong Controller: Static Auditing of Vendor--Protocol Mismatches in LLM-Generated PLC Code
items.summary: arXiv:2611.33227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models can generate Python that drives industrial protocols on programmable logic controllers, yet existing code-grounding checks ask whether an imported package or symbol exists rather than whether it suits the declared industrial target. items.title: Onnx2TEE: Automated Graph-Aware Model Partitioning for TEE-based Edge AI Protection
items.summary: arXiv:2611.33262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI models are increasingly being deployed at the edge. Since these models often require significant research and development to produce, are often deployed in potentially hostile environments, and downstream systems often rely on accurate data; protecting them from theft or manipulation is worthy of serious consideration. items.summary: arXiv:2611.33373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Business commitments require accepted terms to be linked to delegated authority, reserved resources and durable evidence. items.summary: arXiv:2611.33385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-evolving defenses improve LLM-agent security by learning reusable policies from observed attacks. items.summary: arXiv:2611.33453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing complexity of modern hardware designs is making security assurance increasingly difficult. One of the foundational steps in pre-silicon security verification is identifying security assets. While primary assets are often evident from design functionality, the internal signals that can facilitate their compromise are much less apparent. items.summary: arXiv:2611.33519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI coding agents increasingly write and submit code with limited human review, and much of it passes functional tests while remaining insecure. items.summary: arXiv:2611.33595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern cryptographic protocols such as WPA2-PSK, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), and Bluetooth Classic (BC) tolerate low-entropy keys for user-friendliness, backward compatibility, or resource-constrained deployment, yet existing symbolic protocol verifiers rely on the perfect-encryption assumption and therefore cannot reason about brute-force attackers. items.title: The Detour Is the Danger: Preserving Security During LLM Agent Recovery
items.summary: arXiv:2611.33605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on external tools and reusable Skills to execute complex workflows, autonomously replanning when operations fail. However, such recovery may preserve task functionality while silently discarding the security protections required by the original workflow. Existing protections decide who may reach an accelerator or keep its data safe. items.summary: arXiv:2603.10242v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing high performance blockchains verify one signature per transaction on the critical path, which creates O(N) verification cost, high hardware pressure, and difficult post quantum migration. items.summary: arXiv:2603.23670v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multi-chain ecosystems suffer from fragmented identity, siloed liquidity, and bridge-dependent token transfers. items.summary: arXiv:2610.35999v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Microkernels provide good features such as high security, safety, and flexibility, but their reliance on hardware-based isolation leads to heavy performance overhead, limiting their widespread adoption. The security of the scheme (intractability of finding two distinct openings for a given bit using the same commitment) follows from the collision resistance of the hash function. items.title: USN-9209-1: Simple DirectMedia Layer vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Simple DirectMedia Layer incorrectly handled memory when encountering errors during OpenGL ES streaming texture creation. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause applications using Simple DirectMedia Layer to consume resources, resulting in a denial of service.

items.title: USN-9211-1: Plexus Utils vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Plexus Utils did not properly sanitize file paths when extracting archives. If a user or automated system were tricked into extracting a specially crafted archive, an attacker could possibly use this issue to write arbitrary files and execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9208-1: alsa-lib vulnerabilities
items.summary: It was discovered that the ALSA library incorrectly handled certain crafted topology files and control element identifiers. An attacker could possibly use these issues to cause a denial of service or expose sensitive information. These issues were only addressed in Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS.

items.title: USN-9207-1: Apache Commons BCEL vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Apache Commons BCEL incorrectly cached classes under their self-declared names without validating them against the requested name. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause BCEL to return or verify a different class than the one requested.

items.title: PAN-OS Fragnesia exploited; 1Password breach; GeoServer attacks
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks confirms Fragnesia exploitation on PAN-OS devices with exposed management interfaces. 1Password disclosed a GitHub-based breach, and GeoServer flaws are being probed.

items.title: USN-9204-1: dav1d vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that dav1d incorrectly handled certain AV1 video streams with extremely large frame sizes. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause dav1d to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code.

items.title: OmegaLinux 4.0
items.summary: OmegaLinux is an Arch-based, rolling-release Linux distribution featuring the lightweight LXDE desktop. It is suitable for installation on older computers with as little as 1 GB of memory. OmegaLinux was originally based on Lubuntu, but it was rebuilt on top of an Arch Linux base in February 2026.

items.title: NagisinnraLinux 1.1.2
items.summary: NagisinnraLinux is a Japanese Linux distribution based on Debian's "Stable" branch. Featuring a lightweight Xfce desktop, it is specifically designed to revive older hardware and provide a snappy and minimal, yet fully functional desktop environment for daily use. The distribution's main features include out-of-the-box support for the Japanese language, advanced memory optimisation, use of zram compression to guarantee smooth multitasking, and removal of unnecessary and redundant services to maximise battery life and CPU responsiveness.

items.title: Mint 27-beta
items.summary: Linux Mint is an Ubuntu-based distribution whose goal is to provide a classic desktop experience with many convenient, custom tools and optional out-of-the-box multimedia support. It also adds a custom desktop and menus, several unique configuration tools, and a web-based package installation interface. Linux Mint is compatible with Ubuntu software repositories. Besides its Ubuntu-based flavour, the project also produces a separate "Debian" edition (called LMDE), based on the latest stable Debian version.

items.title: FUSS 13.8
items.summary: FUSS is a Debian-based Linux distribution for managing an educational network. It provides server, thin client and desktop solutions based on free software that go beyond any economic or technical reasons, maintaining an ethical choice of freedom and knowledge sharing. FUSS, which stands for "Free Upgrade in South Tyrol's Schools" started in 2005 in Italy's autonomous province of Bolzano/Bozen - South Tyrol, with the aim of bringing free software to schools.

items.title: Clonezilla 3.3.5-3
items.summary: Clonezilla Live is a Debian-based live CD containing Clonezilla, a partition and disk cloning software similar to Norton Ghost. It saves and restores only used blocks in hard drive. With Clonezilla, one can clone a 5 GB system to 40 clients in about 10 minutes.

items.title: Quirinux 2.3_Rev1
items.summary: Quirinux is a Devuan-based Linux distribution designed for the development of animated films. The project provides tools to create an animated film using various common techniques (traditional, digital, cut-out, CGI-3D, stop motion, motion graphics) using open-source software. The distribution uses the Xfce desktop and its main features include ease of installation with the Calamares system installer, GIMP image editor that comes with a configurator tool and extra plugins, and choice of themes and desktop layouts.

items.title: Milis 2026.11.23
items.summary: Milis Linux is an independently-developed Linux distribution supported by Akdeniz University in Antalya, Turkey. It is built using the Linux From Scratch (LFS) project and it includes a custom package management utility called Milis Paket Sistemi (MPS). Milis Linux deploys Wayland as the default graphic server with the labwc window-stacking compositor, the Waybar Wayland bar and Sakura terminal emulator to create a functional desktop user interface.
